correctness.rationale: Stationarity follows from the contraction V law = (1-beta)Z_0²+beta V independent, defining a positive infinite Gaussian quadratic form. All fixed-beta inverse p moments are finite because V dominates a positive multiple of the first n Gaussian squares for any n>2p; the finite-n cutoff follows from polar integration of an n-dimensional Gaussian quadratic form with full-rank positive weights. By Tonelli, M_p=1/Gamma(p) integral_0^infty t^{p-1} prod_{j>=0}(1+2(1-beta)t beta^j)^(-1/2) dt. For noncritical p between successive half-integers, substitute t=beta^{-k}u; the first k factors tend to their power-law limits, the remaining factors to one, and the integrable beta-function majorant yields the exact Gamma expression and exponent. For p=k/2 the same scaling is marginal; change to log-beta time x=log t/log(1/beta). The leading plateau covers one unit interval [k-1,k] with height 2^{-k/2}/Gamma(k/2), tails dominated integrably, producing a single log. The finite startup and beta=0 boundaries are explicitly separated. Independently integrated the Mellin product at beta=1e-3 and 1e-5 for p=.25,.75,1.25: scaled ratios moved toward 1. At critical k=1,2, the two-scale logarithmic slopes match predicted coefficients within 0.54%. Numerical corroboration does not prove dominated-convergence steps.

final_claim: For independent standard Gaussian Z_j, stationary variance V_beta=(1-beta) sum_{j>=0} beta^j Z_j², 0<beta<1, all E[V_beta^{-p}] are finite for every p>0. If k/2<p<(k+1)/2, k=floor(2p), then beta^{kp-k(k+1)/4} E[V_beta^{-p}] tends to 2^{-p}Gamma(p-k/2)Gamma((k+1)/2-p)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma(p)). At p=k/2, integer k>=1, the asymptotic has beta^{-k(k-1)/4} log(1/beta) coefficient 2^{-k/2}/Gamma(k/2). With finite n positive-weight Gaussian terms inverse moment finite iff n>2p; beta=0 permits p<1/2.
